newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar dips in late trade after RBNZ note.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar dips in late trade after RBNZ note.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar took a dip in late Thursday trade but opinion was divided as to whether it was the result of the Reserve Bank's decision to change its approach to assessing monetary conditions.

One dealer said the fall was due to a large sell order while others suggested the market may have read more into the Reserve Bank's note, which said it would not change its judgements on the extent of inflation pressures.
The RBNZ said its monetary policy statement, due on June 27, would no longer assume nominal interest rates and the exchange rate to be constant.
"Instead the statement will show inflation returning to near the middle of the 0-3 percent target range and a path for how monetary conditions may need to evolve to achieve this," the bank said.
Many dealers said it was a complex technical issue.
"But I guess you can read something into it," said one.

"They are forecasting an inflation rate to be between zero and three percent, ie 1.5. If we look at their current forecasts, they are at about 0.8, so therefore it's about 0.7 percent of interest rate movement available to ease from here. That's the speculation," he said.
Others were confident that the Reserve Bank did not mean anything through its announced changes and so they were quite confident holding long positions.
By 4.45 p.m. (0445 GMT) the Kiwi was at 0.6856/63, down from 0.6772 just before the announcement and substantially off its peak of 0.6885. The currency started the session at 0.6879/86.
On its trade weighted index, the Kiwi slumped to 67.46 from 67.69 at the open. The Monetary Conditions Index widened out to minus 0.91 basis point equivalent from minus 0.77.

One analyst said the Kiwi, which had been in a downtrend all week, appeared to have been hit by a large sell order from one bank. "And the thing has been sliding all week on the back of the Aussie," he said.
